Authored only from trusted_evidence_spec.md (005-Y revision: 부분의 자기 코드 검사, a choice part whose answer does not name its own choice_part while the cited record names it is asked once more with choice_retry and then gets a notice quoting the first sentence naming that code, contract still v18; and an answer text that two parts both gave is joined once; with the 005-X choice parts and value check, the 005-W choice_codes, the 005-V choice_retry, the 005-U conflict_records, the 005-T status retry, the 005-S cap and 005-R two-case paragraphs, the sub-code and situation splits and section 6); the 005-X acceptance suite was read for format only (schema, case keys, registry shape, the expected block, how split and choice cases list model_statuses, mention-group and forbidden-pattern notation), the gate v20 constants, validate_suite and registry_for for structure, the 005-X manifest thresholds, and evidence_registry for content_sha256 and record_problems. No implementation, run output, test, review file or other suite's expected results were read, the pipeline was not run, and all questions, records and patterns were written fresh; other suites were searched only for duplicate questions, status codes and reused names. Focus, choice questions (spec 4 and 5, 005-X/005-Y): two sibling sub-codes with a choosing word and one admissible record naming both, so the question gets choice_codes and is split into one part per choice code in question order; model_statuses lists one status per part. Choice cases, one per category, two per question language: A05Y-02 (vi, right code second, own-sentence values), A05Y-22 (en, right code second, own-sentence values, historical date with a not-yet-effective successor), A05Y-33 (vi, right code first, own-sentence values, also a not-conflict), A05Y-45 (ko question, English evidence, right code first, own-sentence values), A05Y-62 (en, right code second, one shared sentence naming both codes with what each covers and no value), A05Y-70 (ko, right code second, one shared classification sentence 전문학사 → N-4-1, 일반학사 → N-4-2, no value). In A05Y-62 and A05Y-70 a part could answer only the right code; the 005-Y self-code check and its quoting notice are the guard there, and the raw mention groups (both codes and both class words) catch such an answer. Choice questions ask a comparison or a classification rather than quoting a value. Choice near-misses: A05Y-18 (a sub-code with its own parent N-4), A05Y-58 (second code R-9 never named by the evidence), A05Y-60 (two codes without a choosing word), A05Y-81 (a choosing question whose records are each limited to one sub-code, so the 005-J sub-code split applies and each part gets only its own record and no choice_codes). Kept from 005-X: conflict-template cases A05Y-28, 29, 30, 44, 56, 59, 67 (28, 29, 30, 44, 67 ask what each text says); not-conflicts A05Y-31, 32, 33; partial traps A05Y-36, 42, 61; cap positives A05Y-01, 03, 37; two-case positives A05Y-16, 40, 43; role reversal A05Y-14, 25, 78. Ambiguities recorded: (1) Spec 4 (005-X) says each part writes what the evidence says about its choice_part and whether that code is the one sought; with a shared classification sentence the part for the non-matching code states the class that code covers and that it is not the one sought, so the joined first answer carries both codes and both class words, which are the mention groups. (2) Spec 6 lists missing item names and missing 005-R cases as what a notice can fill; spec 5 (005-V, reused by 005-Y) also scores the end-to-end channel on the released answer plus its notice, so a 'one code' answer fails the raw mention groups but can pass end-to-end through the notice that quotes the missing code's sentence. (3) The 005-Y join-once rule compares the part texts exactly; two parts that differ by a character are both kept. (4) Spec 5 (005-X) reads numbers taken from the question as possible swapped values; A05Y-22's question date (2025-09-20) shares no number with a code sentence, and no other choice question carries a number. (5) 'or', 'hay' and 'nào' also occur inside other words (for, thay); every question with two sibling codes either has a whole-word choosing word or is Korean with no Latin letters (A05Y-60), and every other 'or' sits in a question with at most one sibling code. (6) No forbidden pattern binds a value to a code; value patterns forbid inadmissible values only, and choice patterns fire only on a stated conclusion naming the wrong code (sentences with a negation, contrast word or the right code are skipped); each was tested against value-first correct answers in all three languages. (7) Mention groups assume the 005-S normalisation (lower case, whitespace removed).
